records.name: Lutheran Settlement House Qigong Class
records.summary: A weekly qigong class for adults 55 and up at the Lutheran Settlement House in Fishtown, with slow movement, breathing, and meditation.
records.what_you_do: Move through qigong postures and breathing exercises with others your age, at any skill level.

cost.text: No fee is listed on the page

first_step.how: Come to a Thursday class. No registration is needed.
first_step.basis: The page says all skill levels are welcome and no sign up is needed

records.notes: Kind set to program because it is run by a settlement house. A search summary dated the class July 2026; I used only the page's own listing of the October 8, 2026 session.

records.name: Zen Center of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Zen meditation community for everyday people, with sittings in person and on Zoom and a monthly day-long sitting.
records.what_you_do: Sit zazen with the group, get instruction as a first-time visitor, and join a monthly day-long sesshin if you want.

schedule.text: Sundays 10 am to noon and Wednesdays 7 to 8 pm, in person or online. Weekday mornings 7 to 8 am on Zoom only.

cost.text: Donations and membership are invited. No fee amounts are on the home page.

first_step.how: Email zencenterphiladelphia@gmail.com for the Zoom link or to ask about visiting
first_step.basis: The page says beginners are welcome and first-time visitors receive instruction

records.notes: The sitting schedule looks current but is undated. The newest dated item I could find is a July 2023 sesshin listing, so status is dormant by the dated-evidence rule. Verify before showing as active. The home page has no street address; a search snippet gave one but I did not verify it on the group's site, so it is left out.

records.name: The Philadelphia Meditation Center
records.notes: Meets at 8 East Eagle Road, Havertown (Delaware County), outside city limits. The site does not say it recruits Philadelphia residents specifically, so it is not published. Schedule seen: Wednesday and Sunday evenings, Saturday mornings, and a monthly daylong. Contact phlmedctr@aol.com, 610.853.8200.

records.name: Delaware Valley Insight Meditation
records.summary: A peer-led Insight meditation community across Southeastern Pennsylvania, South Jersey, and Northern Delaware, with local sitting groups you can join by email.
records.what_you_do: Join a local sitting group near you, or ask for help starting one in your area.

schedule.text: Local sitting groups set their own times. The site lists no schedule.

first_step.how: Use the Join A Sitting Group page to get on the mailing list for your area
first_step.basis: Open to people of all backgrounds and abilities with a clear sign up path. The site does not mention beginners by name.

records.notes: No dated news or events on the site. The only dated mention is a 2023 biographical note, which is not evidence of activity, so status is unknown. Email is the contact published for starting a new group.

records.name: West Philly Insight
records.summary: A free weekly meditation class in West Philadelphia, open to anyone, that meets at Calvary Community Center on Baltimore Avenue.
records.what_you_do: Sit and meditate with the group in the Insight style, and take part in the weekly class.

schedule.text: Weekly meditation classes. The days and times are on the group's schedule page, which I could not read.

cost.text: Classes are offered freely. No donation policy is stated.

first_step.how: Email westphillyinsight@gmail.com to ask about the next class
first_step.basis: The site says the classes are open to everyone and invites newcomers, with an email for questions

records.notes: A working site with no dated items, so status is probably_active. Days and times live on a schedule page I could not read; check before publishing a weekday.

records.name: Tai Chi in the Square (Franklin Square Tai Chi Group)
records.summary: A free morning tai chi group that practices outdoors at Franklin Square, open to everyone.
records.what_you_do: Practice tai chi outdoors with the group, and move to the pavilion when the weather is cold or wet.

schedule.text: Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays, 7:30 to 8:30 am

locations.label: Franklin Square, northeast side of the fountain

first_step.how: Go to the northeast side of the fountain at Franklin Square at class time, or join the group's Facebook page
first_step.basis: The page says all are welcome at a set place and time. It does not say beginners are welcome by name.

records.notes: The page shows only the recurring weekly schedule, with no event dates. The May 2024 image upload date is not used as evidence. Group is run with Historic Philadelphia's listing.

records.name: Philadelphia Alliance for Labor Support (PALS)
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives free doula support during labor to people who could not otherwise get it, and offers subsidized doula training.
records.what_you_do: Trained volunteer doulas support families through labor and birth. Newer doulas take the subsidized training.

schedule.text: Doula training is offered twice a year. Dates are not on the website.

cost.text: Doula support is free to families. Training is subsidized.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer with PALS or Become a Doula links on palsdoulas.com
first_step.basis: Volunteering needs trained doula status or training, and the page does not say what the steps are

records.notes: The site has no dated items and does not list training dates, meeting times, or an email. The Penn student club page for PALS returned a not found error when I checked, so I did not use its contact emails. Confirm volunteer openings directly with the group.

records.name: Action Wellness
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit with a Buddy Program that volunteers can join to offer one-to-one support to people with a chronic illness.
records.what_you_do: Apply to become a buddy, then offer one-to-one support and friendship to people the program serves.

schedule.text: The Buddy Program schedule is set with the group after you apply. The website does not list it.

first_step.how: Use the Apply Now page on the website, or call the office
first_step.basis: The Buddy Program takes an application, and the website does not explain what a buddy does day to day

records.notes: The site confirms the Buddy Program and the office, but does not describe it. The chronic illness and HIV context comes from search results (press coverage and a volunteer listing), not from the group's site, so the summary is kept general. Do not add the volunteer listing's visit schedule or age rule unless the group's site confirms them. The only dated text on the site is a copyright year.

records.name: Philly LIFTS
records.summary: A City of Philadelphia program that links families affected by substance use to support groups, recovery help, doula referrals, and free overdose prevention training.
records.what_you_do: Families get referrals and support groups. Community events and overdose prevention training are open to all families, not only those enrolled.

schedule.text: Support groups and events are listed on the program's events page. The program page gives no days or times.

cost.text: The page does not say whether services cost money

first_step.how: Call the new mothers' support group contact at (215) 776-4406, or complete the intake surveys linked on the page for mental health support
first_step.basis: A public city program with named staff to call, though it does not describe how a first meeting works

records.notes: A city program, not a volunteer group, so families are the audience. Volunteer roles are not described. The city's paid community doula program was seen in search results but is not a volunteer route; it is not written as a separate record. The page has no dated items and no cost.

records.name: Healthy Minds Philly
records.notes: A city behavioral health initiative with free screenings, training, naloxone, a resource blog, and an events calendar. It is a resource, not a group people join. Its listed support groups are single calendar entries with no ongoing schedule, so none are written as records. Worth a look for a future mental health pass.

notes: Ran through the 10 WebSearch budget (the cap) and used 17 WebFetch calls. Records: 8 publish, 1 out_of_area, 1 not_a_group. Small count is because many list results were undated, out of area, or had no group site to check. Drops with reasons: Unitarian Society of Germantown Breathe mindfulness class (named only in a 2020 listing; the congregation's current site does not mention it, so not written). Free Library tai chi and qigong sessions are one-off library events, not groups, so not written. Hospital systems (CHOP, Penn, Jefferson, Main Line) are institutional volunteer offices, not groups; their pages are leads. Biggest gaps: Prevention Point and NAMI (blocked), and no verified neighborhood coverage for Northeast Philadelphia in health-wellness. Several Zen and PALS facts are from pages with no dates; confidence is set low for those. Not done: the Shambhala and Nalandabodhi centers, Monarch Yoga and Yoga 4 Philly (no URLs captured for most).
